tier: 1 Year personal plan, $180.00 per year ($15.00 per month)

free_tier.stated: No free tier. The pricing page lists three personal plans: '1 Month $30.00 per month', '1 Year $15.00 per month, Pay $180.00 every year' and '2 Years $12.50 per month, Pay $300.00 every 2 years'. Every plan includes 'Unlimited bandwidth & server switches'.
free_tier.notes: The cheapest yearly price is $180.00 for a 1 Year term; the page prints a struck-through list price of $360.00 and a 'Save 50%' label. The page also shows a reseller-coupon banner; the prices above are the plan cards. Private IP is a paid add-on at $5.00 per month each and the VIP add-on starts at $10 per month.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an exit address, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: No object is stored. The constraints are the port-forwarding scope and the P2P server set in limits.

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel and a rented exit address, not stored bytes

egress.terms: The pricing page states 'Unlimited bandwidth & server switches' for every plan and no byte allowance or overage price. metered is false on that statement; no byte was counted through a tunnel.
egress.free_allowance: none published: the pages price a term, not a volume

interface_detail: Vendor apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android and a router applet; OpenVPN and WireGuard also work from third-party clients per the protocol page (OpenWeb and StealthVPN only from the vendor's software). The vendor provides no SOCKS5 endpoint of its own, so there is no proxy URL to dial. No interface term names a VPN tunnel.
tooling: The vendor's desktop and mobile apps, or an OpenVPN or WireGuard client for the open protocols; the vendor's router applet for port forwarding on a router. A SOCKS5 or HTTP client has nothing to connect to: the vendor says it supplies no SOCKS5 settings or credentials.
chaining: A compute node runs the vendor's Linux app or an OpenVPN or WireGuard client, so all of its traffic leaves at the chosen server's address; a Worker cannot dial the tunnel directly, and there is no proxy endpoint to hand it.

limits.value: Port forwarding only on star-marked servers: one pre-selected port on a shared IP, all ports or selected ports on a dedicated IP; BitTorrent and P2P only on star-marked P2P servers
none: 'Unlimited bandwidth & server switches' on every plan

limits_note: Port forwarding and P2P are both confined to servers marked with a star in the app, so a BitTorrent session needs a P2P server and a forwarded port needs a (possibly different) selected server. The 'Connect unlimited devices in your household' line is a household wording, not a number. The SOCKS5 row is a documented absence: the vendor's blog says it does not provide SOCKS5 proxy settings or credentials.
binding_note: No byte quota exists ('Unlimited bandwidth'), so the constraint that binds first for a client is the star-marked server set that carries port forwarding and P2P; no rate was measured.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form on the pricing page asks for 'Your name', 'Your e-mail', password and confirm password, an ALTCHA check, then 'We have sent you a confirmation message with a sign-up link'; it lists Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, American Express, Cirrus, PayPal, Bitcoin, Monero and bank transfer as payment methods. No phone number or identity document is asked on the form. A card is one option among cryptocurrencies, so the structured kind is email.

reliability_note: Which servers are P2P is shown only in the app and its server list, so the P2P set is unverified beyond the star convention. unverified: no exit-IP registry class was measured.
confidence_note: Documented from the vendor's pricing, protocol, port-forwarding and wiki pages as served. Measured would need a paid account, the cheapest term bought, a tunnel brought up per protocol and the star-marked server set counted.

evidence.proved: The 1 Year plan is billed $180.00 every year (list price struck through at $360.00); the 2 Years plan is $300.00 every 2 years.
The 1 Year plan is shown as $15.00 per month; the 1 Month plan is $30.00 per month and the 2 Years plan $12.50 per month.
Protocols included in every plan: OpenVPN, StealthVPN, OpenWeb and WireGuard.
Every plan includes unlimited bandwidth and server switches.
Sign-up asks for name, e-mail and password with a confirm-password field; the form's other elements are an ALTCHA check and a Create account button.

evidence.quote: We have sent you a confirmation message with a sign-up link.
evidence.proved: After the form the sign-up needs an e-mail confirmation link before the account continues.

evidence.quote: StealthVPN is another proprietary protocol by Astrill. It is inspired by OpenVPN and performs an additional obfuscation of traffic which makes it undetectable for automated firewall systems.
evidence.proved: StealthVPN is the obfuscated protocol: OpenVPN-derived, extra traffic obfuscation, and available only with the vendor's software.

evidence.quote: StealthVPN is very stable and it can work with both UDP and TCP modes.
evidence.proved: StealthVPN runs over both UDP and TCP.

evidence.quote: OpenWeb is very hard to detect by DPI (deep packet inspection).
evidence.proved: OpenWeb is a TCP, DPI-resistant proprietary protocol (obfuscation).

evidence.quote: Astrill VPN allows its users to forward certain ports on selected highly secure servers.
evidence.proved: Port forwarding exists only on selected servers marked with a star in the app.

evidence.quote: If you have a shared IP address, Astrill enables you to forward one pre-selected port.
evidence.proved: On a shared IP address one pre-selected port is forwarded.

evidence.quote: VPN Servers which allows P2P/Torrent/eMule/eDonkey traffic are marked with a star in Astrill application and Servers List.
evidence.proved: BitTorrent and other P2P traffic is carried on star-marked P2P servers in the app and server list.

evidence.quote: While AstrillVPN is a powerful tool for securing your connection, please note that AstrillVPN does not provide SOCKS5 proxy settings or credentials.
evidence.proved: The vendor states it provides no SOCKS5 endpoint or credentials of its own.

price_per_tb_month: USD 15.00 per month on the 1 Year plan (USD 180.00 every year); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
notes: The vendor's protocols: OpenVPN, StealthVPN (obfuscated, UDP or TCP), OpenWeb (TCP, DPI-resistant) and WireGuard. Obfuscation is a protocol property here (StealthVPN, OpenWeb), not a setting. Port forwarding: Yes, on star-marked servers: one pre-selected port on a shared IP, all ports or selected ports on a dedicated IP; works with desktop apps and the router applet. BitTorrent rule: Allowed on star-marked P2P servers: 'VPN Servers which allows P2P/Torrent/eMule/eDonkey traffic are marked with a star'.
